decisions.rationale: 'adenomatous polyposis coli' names one specific hereditary disease with no further categorization, so it is a Specific Disease in the title. Duplicate mentions in the title and abstract are each annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate §4 (Annotate duplicate mentions)

decisions.rationale: 'adenomatous polyposis coli' in the abstract is the named disease, the dominantly inherited syndrome, and is annotated as a Specific Disease. It is a duplicate of the title mention and is annotated separately.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate §4 (Annotate duplicate mentions)

decisions.rationale: 'APC' is the abbreviation defined in parentheses after 'adenomatous polyposis coli' and refers to the same specific disease. Abbreviation and long form are annotated as separate mentions.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §6 (Synonymous mentions / abbreviation definitions)

decisions.rationale: 'colorectal tumourigenesis' refers to a biological process (tumour formation), not a disease name, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §5 (references to biological processes)

decisions.rationale: 'disease' is a very general term used in 'family history of the disease' and is excluded.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §4 (general terms such as 'disease')

decisions.rationale: 'cancer' is retained by the guidelines. As a generic term covering a family of many specific diseases, it is a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §4 (the terms 'cancer' and 'tumor' are retained); What to Annotate §1 (Disease Class)

decisions.rationale: 'APC' in 'unselected APC patients' is a disease name used adjectivally to modify the noun 'patients', so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: 'condition' is a general term that refers to the disease only indirectly and is not a specific disease name, so it is excluded.
